# Run On Manual Request Clause

A connected task-launch policy whose `request` action creates a tracked work request. Acceptance records an intention to perform work; it does not establish that the work started or completed.

## Configuration and triggering

`parameters.workClause` defaults to `work`. It must name a Task Work Clause in the same document, and that clause must match `/taskWork/ownerClause`. The launch function checks the policy type, the exact work-clause type and ledger ownership before accepting a request.

Configure named connections under `bindings.request`. These are action connections, not data bindings. No automatic connection is declared. The launch function accepts only `on: workflow` and `on: initialized`; the latter responds to Clauses Initialized despite this type's manual-request name. Other source modes are rejected when they reach the launch function.

A workflow connection uses `party`, when supplied, otherwise `channel`, to name its authenticated channel. Its optional `request` pattern constrains the call payload, and `event` can filter the connection. The configured channel determines who may invoke it; this clause fixes no launching actor. Clause, connection and workflow-channel names must be nonempty and contain no `.`, `/` or `~`. Changing an installed connection configuration requires a new clause key.

Connection `params` supplies the action arguments and defaults to `{}`. `params.input` becomes the emitted request's `input`; `/instructions` supplies its `instructions`. The workflow call payload is available as `trigger` and is not automatically copied into `params`. This action declares no input schema or input default.

A connection's `when` defaults to true; false skips the action. `parameters.conditions.request`, if supplied, must pass or the attempt fails. `once` defaults to false. When true, it suppresses later invocations after that connection has accepted a new request and completed its configured `after` steps. Configured `before` steps precede the request function; `after` steps follow its `acceptedNew` outcome.

## Acceptance and recorded outcomes

The owning Task Work Clause initializes `/taskWork/nextRequestNumber` to 1. Each accepted launch allocates a new `request-N` identifier, advances the sequence, adds a `pending` entry to `taskWork.requests`, stores an exact reference to the request, and emits Task Work Requested with `requestId`, `input` and `instructions`. The helper returns `acceptedNew` and `requestId` to the action's `outcome-v1` check. Repeated inputs are not deduplicated, and pending work does not itself prevent another launch.

An unsupported launch mode or invalid work owner rejects the launch attempt; it does not create a reported task failure. Likewise, the connection's `fired` flag records once-only launch acceptance, not successful task performance. With `once: false`, accepted launches do not set that flag.

The owning Task Work Clause accepts correlated reports through its `performer` channel. A successful report has status `succeeded` and a required `result` matching its configured `reportRequest` schema. A failure report has status `failed`, a nonempty text `error`, and no `result`. Unknown request identifiers are rejected.

A newly accepted report changes the request's disposition from `pending` to `succeeded` or `failed`, stores its exact report reference, replaces `/taskWork/latestReport`, and emits Task Report Accepted. Repeating the identical final report returns `alreadyFinal` without replacing the latest report or emitting another acceptance event; a different report for an already-final request is rejected. `/taskWork/latestReport` starts as `{}` after owner initialization and subsequently holds the most recently accepted new report, not an overall task status or necessarily the latest-created request's outcome. Missing state remains unknown.
